page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Page number and running head at the top. Catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.
page.running_head: De Agro Fris. inter Lavic. & Amas.

main_text.p: omnibus æqualiter dicunto ex legibus patriis. Si in eo negligent, aut facere non volent officium suum, Hovetmanni Groningani compellantor, iisque sub pœnâ primum scutatorum x, deinde xx, postremò contumaciæ mandanto, ut jus petentibus expediant: multaque huiusmodi ex semisse civitatis, reliquum Reip. Vpsteranæ esto. Electus prætor aut judex munus annuum non recusato, aut x scutatos Reip. pendito. Prætor judicesque sententiam à se latam petentibus scriptam exhibento.
Ab hac appellandi jus esto, si quis volet, ad Hovetmannos Groninganos intra diem decimum.
Quo rite facto, prior judex non procedito longius: causa refertor ad conventum juredicialem proximum in urbe.

Appellans verò si non persequetur litem in proximo, aut saltem altero conventu, non solum lite cadito, sed etiam marcas quinque multam solvito: nisi forte judex, qui sententiam tulit, ad conventum ipse non veniat: hoc enim appellantem à pœnâ absolvet, judex verò emansitans pœnam pendito. Idem judex & appellans quinas marcas deponunto apud conventum, amittitoque depositum, qui succumbet, victor recipito. Signatum foe-

page.notes: The paragraph division is inferred: the printed lines carry no clear indents, so I split before the marked sentences "Ab hac", "Quo rite" and "Appellans", where a leading mark stands. The mark before "Ab hac", "Quo rite" and "Appellans" is a printed ornament, not text, and is not transcribed. The running head and the long-s letters in "Fris." and "Amas." are read from the scan. The page ends on the hyphenated "foe-" and continues on the next page with the catchword "dus".
